Layer 1: per-row read-modify-write (NOT an atomic bulk UPDATE...WHERE).
For each candidate post, checks status='DRAFT' and publish_status in
('idle','failed') in Python, then assigns a fresh publish_attempt_id and
flips publish_status='pending' via ORM attribute assignment + db.flush().
Posts that fail the check are included in the 'skipped' list with a
human-readable reason. The real idempotency fence against duplicate
publishes is Layer 2 (the Celery task's own CAS UPDATE...WHERE in
``publish_post_task`` — see core/tasks/publish_post.py), not this loop.

LinkedIn/GBP destinations.

Every pre-flight rejection (caption excludes, GBP safety, DRAFT/FAILED
status guard, publish-in-progress guard, avatar face validation, LinkedIn
rate limit, missing destinations) still runs synchronously and is
reflected in THIS response, exactly as before. Once those pass, the
row(s) flip to publish_status=PENDING and are handed to
``publish_post_task`` (the same Celery task ``batch_publish`` uses) —
the actual provider calls, including the up-to-90s Facebook video
transcode wait (``PublishOrchestrator._wait_for_video_ready``), run off
the request/event loop instead of inline here. Previously a video whose
transcode took longer than the client's 60s HTTP timeout looked like a
failure even though the backend published it — and held the single
event-loop worker for up to 90s doing it.

The post must be in DRAFT or FAILED status, and its publish_status must
be idle or failed (not already pending/publishing/published).

    for a multi-platform post) in publish_status=PENDING. Poll

    PUBLISHED (all targets succeeded), stays DRAFT with page_errors set
    (partial success), or becomes FAILED (all targets failed).

         global posts_exclude_text list, the banner failed avatar face
         validation, or the post has no destinations configured.
    429: LinkedIn destination present and the per-user rate limit

    503: Caption safety check is temporarily unavailable, or the publish
         task could not be queued (transient broker/Redis error) — safe

Returns null (HTTP 200) when no Threads account is connected — avoids
browser console 404 noise on every page load for unconnected users.

A connection the platform RETIRED (Threads rejected its token) is returned
with ``is_active=false`` and ``is_expired=true`` instead of null, so the UI
can prompt a reconnect. Returning null for it — the old behaviour — made an
expired grant indistinguishable from never having connected, and the
composer dropped the destination without a word. A disconnect the USER
asked for still returns null: that is a choice, not a failure.

When ``user_id`` is provided (admin with AUTO_POSTS), returns the target
LO's Threads account instead of the caller's — mirrors ``GET
/linkedin/me``. Without it, an admin composing for LO X would put the
ADMIN's ``threads_users.id`` into the post's ``threads_user_ids`` while
``post.user_id`` is X, so the publish resolves X's account, finds no
matching row and fails with THREADS_TOKEN_MISSING.
Target-user-not-found still raises 404 — a real lookup error, not a "not
connected" state.

Note:

Requires: Authorization: Bearer <token>

post.description:
Return the self-contained embed HTML for iframe embedding, seeded with card data.

Requires a valid Bearer token (``Authorization: Bearer <ally-jwt>``).
Returns 401 if the token is absent or invalid.

Note: despite the ``/public`` router prefix, this specific route IS
authenticated.  The slug route in the same file remains fully public.

Accepts a JSON body with ``device`` and ``card`` fields.
The server injects ``window.__EMBED_SEED__ = {device, card}`` into the
returned HTML so the embed bundle can render immediately on first paint
without waiting for a postMessage round-trip.

``card`` is a free-form dict of display fields supplied by the embedder;
the server does not validate its contents — it serialises them verbatim.

The response includes ``Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors *`` so
any host page (web or mobile WebView) may embed it; ``X-Frame-Options``
is intentionally absent.  Cache-Control is omitted because POST responses
vary by body and must not be cached.

get.description:
Return a published LO profile card by slug.

- 200 if the card exists and is published.
- 404 if the slug is unknown or the card is not published.

Return an indexable per-LO crawler document for social/search crawlers.

Emits a canonical link, per-LO ``og:*`` / ``twitter:*`` tags, a meta
description, a schema.org ``Person`` JSON-LD block, and a visible body
with the same facts the SPA card shows — so this page is both a good
social-share preview and a good search-indexable page in its own right.

The canonical/``og:url`` is always built from ``settings.ALLY_APP_URL``
(never the request Host/X-Forwarded-Host header and never
``PUBLIC_MEDIA_HOST``), so a spoofed Host header cannot alter the URL a
crawler indexes.

Every LO-supplied field is HTML-escaped so a hostile value like
``"><script>`` cannot inject markup into the document, and the JSON-LD
block is serialised with ``_script_safe_json`` so it cannot break out of
its ``<script>`` tag either. The page never includes the LO's email.

- 404 (``noindex``, no card data) if the slug is unknown or the card is
  not published.

several LOs can be connected to the same Meta ad account under different
Ally users — see `feedback_meta_token_shared_ad_account` memory).

The permission check (`assert_is_leader`) runs BEFORE the member lookup
below, same ordering as `remind_member_readiness` — a non-leader must
never learn whether `member_user_id` is even a member of this team.

- `assert_teamless` — someone already on a team cannot be creating

post.description:
Generate the Top 1% Loan Officer banner for one officer.

One request, **one job**: the officer's own banner (featured person + contact
block), queued and posted to their own pages. The rank is fixed — this endpoint
is the "TOP 1%" accolade specifically; there is no rank/tier field.

Swagger opens the body below on its **Example Value** tab, which shows one sample
value per field. The permitted values are listed here because that tab does not
show them — the **Schema** tab does.

| Field | Permitted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `region` | free text, 1-60 chars, single line | shown on the banner as-is, e.g. `CALIFORNIA` or `NATIONWIDE` |
| `award_year` | `2000` to the current year | |
| `metric` | `TOTAL_LOAN_AMOUNT`, `TOTAL_LOANS_CLOSED` | dollar volume, or number of loans closed |
| `lf_id`, `lo_name`, `nmls_id`, `avatar` | required | `avatar` is base64 (data-URL prefix accepted) |
| `phone`, `email`, `website`, `licensed_states` | optional | the contact block draws a row only for a value that is present |

Requests are de-duplicated for 10 minutes on `(api_name, lf_id, body minus avatar)`,
so re-running the same award returns the original `job_id` rather than a new banner.

Generate the Top 3 Loan Officers banners for one award period.

One request, **three jobs**: each winner gets their own banner (the same
featured-person treatment as Top 1%), queued and posted to that officer's own
pages. The response lists one `{lf_id, job_id, message}` per winner; a winner
whose event is switched off gets `job_id: null` and a message, the other two
still run. The rank is not drawn on the banner — every winner receives the
same "TOP 3 ..." accolade; the caption says where they placed.

Swagger opens the body below on its **Example Value** tab, which shows one sample
value per field. The permitted values are listed here because that tab does not
show them — the **Schema** tab does.

| Field | Permitted values | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `scope` | `COMPANY`, `STATE` | `STATE` requires `region`; `COMPANY` leaves it unset |
| `period` | `MONTHLY`, `QUARTERLY`, `YEARLY` | decides which of `period_month` / `period_quarter` is required |
| `metric` | `TOTAL_LOAN_AMOUNT`, `TOTAL_LOANS_CLOSED` | dollar volume, or number of loans closed |
| `period_month` | `1`-`12` | required when `period` is `MONTHLY`, omit otherwise |
| `period_quarter` | `1`-`4` | required when `period` is `QUARTERLY`, omit otherwise |
| `award_year` | `2000` to the current year | |
| `winners` | exactly 3 entries | `rank` 1, 2 and 3, each with `lf_id`, `lo_name`, `nmls_id`, `avatar`, plus optional `phone`, `email`, `website`, `licensed_states` for the contact block |

Each winner's job is de-duplicated for 10 minutes on `(api_name, lf_id, body minus avatar)`,
so re-running the same award returns the original `job_id`s rather than new banners.

or the default frontend settings URL, with
?status=connected&provider=<provider>&email=<email> appended (using '&'
instead of '?' if the base already carries a query string).

When the flow was started by the hosted connect page on behalf of ANOTHER
app (`GET /email-accounts/connect`), the browser goes back to THAT app's
return_url instead — re-checked against the admin allowlist here, since
the origin may have been removed while the user sat on the consent screen.

no ``code``. ``code`` used to be required, so that answered a raw 422 JSON
page instead of taking the user back; it now takes the failure redirect.

check) because the user arrives on a top-level redirect from the OAuth
provider, with no Authorization header to present. State verification
provides the CSRF protection; /email-accounts/oauth/{provider}/start (or
/email-accounts/connect) is the only way to obtain a valid state.

CreateTeamAdGroupRequest.title: CreateTeamAdGroupRequest
CreateTeamAdGroupRequest.description:
Leader-submitted request to create one ad per named member.

Carries every `CreateCampaignRequest` field EXCEPT `page_id`,
`daily_budget_cents`, `launch_immediately`, `locations`, `radius_miles`,
`custom_audience_ids`, `excluded_custom_audience_ids`, and
`landing_page_url` — those eight vary per member and are supplied via
`members` / `to_campaign_request` instead.

Locations are per member (not shared across the group): each member runs
their own copy in their own area, and the wizard warns when that area is
outside the member's own `lo_profile.licensed_states` (from MCP). A
location outside the licence is not refused.

Custom audiences are per member for a different reason: a Meta Custom
Audience lives inside ONE ad account (`act_<id>`), so an audience id
valid on the leader's account is invalid on every other member's — a
shared group-level id would fail Meta's ad-set create for everyone but
the leader. `interests` stays shared (Meta's global taxonomy works on any
account); media/lead-form/CTA/duration stay shared because they are
either re-uploaded per account or otherwise account-agnostic.

`landing_page_url` joined locations and custom audiences as a per-member
field for a third reason: a TRAFFIC ad sends its clicks to the
ADVERTISER's own website, and every member of a group is a different
advertiser. Shared, it pointed every member's ad — and so every member's
traffic — at the leader's own domain.

UpdateSocialLinkRequest.title: UpdateSocialLinkRequest
UpdateSocialLinkRequest.description:
Schema for updating a social link's URL.

For ALLY_BACKEND links: pass only `url` and the existing row will be
updated in place.
For AI_MCP_SERVER links: pass `url` (the new URL) plus `mcp_link_data`
describing the original MCP link being replaced. The backend will
soft-delete-track the original MCP entry and insert a new ALLY_BACKEND
row carrying the edited URL — same pattern as the DELETE endpoint.

VideoEmailCreateIn.title: VideoEmailCreateIn
VideoEmailCreateIn.description:
Request body for creating a new video record.

Everything is optional: the composer creates the draft the moment it
opens, before the LO has typed anything, so the subject (``title``) may
be empty and the CTA falls back to "Reply to {sender}" → mailto the
owner (see ``VideoEmailService.create_draft``).

VideoEmailListStatusFilter.title: VideoEmailListStatusFilter
VideoEmailListStatusFilter.description:
Values accepted by the ``status`` query param on ``GET /video-emails``.

``uploading``/``processing``/``failed`` map straight to the DB column;
``ready``/``sent``/``scheduled``/``draft`` are derived (see
``VideoEmailRepository._list_filters``) and have no column of their own.
Draft / Scheduled / Sent are three DISJOINT statuses in the library:
``draft`` is everything neither sent nor scheduled, ``scheduled`` is its
own status, and ``sent`` is unchanged.

VideoEmailReuseIn.title: VideoEmailReuseIn
VideoEmailReuseIn.description:
POST /video-emails/{id}/reuse — copy parts of ``source_id`` into this draft.

Each flag is one checkbox in the composer's picker. ``content`` is the
subject, message, video-page button and the business-card setting;
``recipients`` is To/Cc/Bcc; ``video`` is the recording (copied, never
shared — see ``VideoEmailService.reuse_from``).

VideoEmailSendIn.title: VideoEmailSendIn
VideoEmailSendIn.description:
Request body for sending a video — ONE email with To/Cc/Bcc.

Gmail's own model: a single provider call, not one per recipient.

VideoEmailUpdateIn.title: VideoEmailUpdateIn
VideoEmailUpdateIn.description:
Request body for PATCH /video-emails/{id} — every field optional.

Lengths mirror the `video_emails` columns (title varchar(255), cta_label
varchar(64)); an untyped dict let a `null` title or an over-long
cta_label through to Postgres and surface as a 500.

VideoEmailUploadCompleteIn.title: VideoEmailUploadCompleteIn
VideoEmailUploadCompleteIn.description: Finalize an upload session (etag / session data depends on protocol).

VideoEmailUploadInitIn.title: VideoEmailUploadInitIn
VideoEmailUploadInitIn.description:
Optional request body for POST /video-emails/{id}/upload-init.

Omitted entirely by the recorder's existing call (webcam/screen capture
is always a WebM container), so every field defaults to today's
behaviour. A device upload from a phone/desktop file picker sends its
real container so the resumable session — and the raw object's
Content-Type in storage — matches what was actually picked, instead of
always claiming "video/webm".
